results.content:
President Donald Trump's approval rating among white voters in Florida has fallen to the edge of negative territory, a striking reversal in a state and demographic group that helped power his return to the White House.

Data displayed by the Civiqs public opinion tracker showed that 47% of white Floridians approved of Trump's job performance as of Sept. 17, while 46% disapproved. Another 7% said they neither approved nor disapproved. [...] At the beginning of Trump's second term, the Civiqs chart placed his approval among white Floridians above 60%, with disapproval in the mid-30s. The lines have moved steadily toward each other since then, leaving a gap of more than 25 points nearly erased.
results.title: Trump's Support Among White Floridians Nears a Historic Reversal

Civiqs, a nonpartisan online polling firm that surveys presidential approval on a rolling basis, puts Trump’s current approval in Idaho at 49 percent, with 41 percent disapproving as of Thursday. That figure has fluctuated near that line in recent weeks. The Idaho Democratic Party cited the same Civiqs data in a statement released Aug. 19. [...] The shift marks a significant change in a state Trump carried by more than 36 percentage points in the 2024 presidential election and where his approval stood well above 50 percent for most of his second term. Wyoming, North Dakota and West Virginia are currently the only other states where Trump holds a positive approval rating above 50 percent.

## What is Trump's approval rating in Tennessee?

Civiqs polls, last updated Sept. 15, indicate Trump's approval in Tennessee has dropped since mid-August after a moderate drop in July.

For the first time in either of his two terms, Trump has a negative approval rating in Tennessee: 44% of residents approve of his performance, 48% disapprove, and 8% are neutral. This equates to a 4-point negative net approval rating, the difference between approval and disapproval ratings. [...] At the beginning of September, Civiqs recorded Trump with a net approval rating of 1% in the state, and that figure has since flipped to -4% as of Sept. 12.
